messages.subject: Re: batchProcess method
messages.body_plain:
Hi Paco,

Currently, only normalize, smoothSignal, reduceBaseline, and peakPick are supported in batchProcess. Performing peakAlign, peakFilter, or reduceDimension must be done separately. After running batchProcess with peakPick, you should be able to do peakAlign and then peakFilter on it afterward. However doing peakAlign afterward is best done using the original object as the reference (with 'ref=') due to some behavior differences (see below).

In addition to streamlining processing steps, a major reason I wanted to add batchProcess was to make it feasible to process larger-than-memory datasets. This was impossible before, even using 'attach.only=TRUE' because normalize, smoothSignal, and reduceBaseline would all produce an output object as larger as the original dataset. So I wanted to add a batchProcess so these could be streamlined with peakPick or reduceDimension so the output object could feasibly fit into memory.

(For this reason, batchProcess doesn't preserve the original spectra after peak picking. Unlike peakPick, the spectra are output as a sparse matrix format instead of being preserved until peakAlign is called. This is to avoid ever duplicating the full original dataset, and why the original object should be used as a reference when doing peakAlign instead of relying on the default behavior. I realize now this behavior is undocumented. I will need to document this.)

While writing batchProcess, I ran up against the Bioconductor 3.3 deadline, so I only managed to implement the current version for this release cycle. Figuring out the best way to incorporate peakAlign and reduceDimension into batchProcess proved to be slightly complicated due to the fact that they couldn't rely on the features being the same as the original dataset at that point in the batch processing. (This isn't a problem for the standalone methods, since the full dataset as always available, but with batchProcess I can't rely on the original object metadata matching the processed spectral data, or the full dataset being available, at any single point during processing.)

So I'm embarrassed to say that 'batchProcess' is slightly "unfinished" for this release cycle. I hope to add support for peakAlign and reduceDimension for the next release by the end of the year. For now, you must call peakAlign separately, preferably explicitly giving the original object as the reference.

-Kylie

messages.subject: Re: Exporting Data While Maintaining Clusters
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jennifer,

This will plot the mean of all the pixels in a segmentation in R, you can vary the plot arguments for color / overlay, etc.:
##kidney_sa: original data
##kidney_sa.peaks : peakdata

##segmentation:
sscg_sa <- spatialShrunkenCentroids(kidney_sa.peaks,r=1,k=10,s=1)

##plot spectra by SSCG class:
plot(kidney_sa,pixel=1:ncol(kidney_sa),pixel.groups=sscg_sa$classes[[1]],fun=mean)

To get the numerical values use:

featureApply(kidney_sa,.pixel.groups=sscg_sa$classes[[1]],.fun=mean)

which will return a matrix of cluster vs m/z bin with intensity values.

Cardinal doesn't currently do any exporting, but you can coerce these mean spectra into  a MALDIquant spectrum object and export MzML files for them as shown below:

##need the MALDIquant package:

require(MALDIquant)
require(MALDIquantForeign)

##get mean cluster data as data.frame:

mean_df <- data.frame(featureApply(kidney_sa,.pixel.groups=sscg_sa$classes[[1]],.fun=mean))

##coerce mean specs to MALDIquant:

SegmentsMzMls <- lapply(c(1:sscg_sa$k[[1]]),function(x){
  spec <-createMassSpectrum(mass=mz(kidney_sa.peaks), intensity=as.numeric(mean_df[x,]))
  return(spec)
})

##write MzMl..

exportMzMl(SegmentsMzMls[[1]], file="segment_1_meanspec.mzml")

##write all MzMl via for loop..

for (i in 1:sscg_sa$k[[1]]){
  exportMzMl(SegmentsMzMls[[i]], file=paste0("segment_",i,"_meanspec.mzml"))
}

Hope that helps.

Heath

messages.subject: Quick-TRANSfer warning
messages.body_plain:
That's a warning from the FORTRAN code in R's built-in kmeans function, which is used to initialize the segmentation. I've never noticed it to have an effect on the final results.

-Kylie
